diagnosis.root_cause: A shared splitter path on EPON0/6 has failed or degraded, leaving at least five ONUs offline while other ONUs on the same PON port remain online.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds successfully with online:0 for ONU indices 15, 16, 19, 20, and 46; this is definite offline status, not a monitoring timeout.
Four other ONUs on EPON0/6 respond online with healthy RX power and normal TX power, proving the PON port is not wholly down.
Two or more definite ONU negatives with surviving ONUs on the same port place the fault boundary inside the port and identify a splitter failure.
The subscriber's stored zero RX/TX values are no readings because the ONU is offline; they do not indicate strong optics.

The seven-day optical telemetry was stable around -22.4 to -23.1 dBm with normal TX power, flat distance at 294 m, and healthy TX bias, so there is no evidence of fibre degradation, laser degradation, or distance change on this customer's path before the dropout.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and OID queries, and its CPU, memory, temperature, and other PON ports are healthy; this rules out an OLT-wide or OLT hardware failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy, the expected VLAN 1016 is present, and RADIUS records are consistent, so authentication, VLAN provisioning, router, and service-session faults are not the cause.
The OLT population has 25 offline customers, but the direct port probe shows the affected boundary and takes precedence over population-based estimates.

remediation.action: Dispatch field operations to test the EPON0/6 splitter and downstream fibre branches, inspect connectors and splices, and repair or replace the failed splitter/branch. Verify that all affected ONUs re-register and restore optical readings afterward.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
